questions: Section 10 refers private aviation to underwriting judgement. For a private pilot who flies no aerobatics, what is the house practice: is the exposure charged as a debit, as a flat extra per $1,000, handled with an aviation exclusion rider, or taken without charge?
What thresholds on hours flown per year and total logged hours does the house use to grade private-pilot risk, and what charge (debit figure or flat-extra band per $1,000) attaches to each grade?
When a private pilot is charged, is an aviation exclusion rider used in place of the flat extra or debit, and if so under what circumstances is the rider used rather than the charge?

Section 16 refers combinations of cardiac risk factors to judgement. Does a 57-year-old male with untreated blood pressure of 135/84, an A1c of 6.0 with no diabetes diagnosis, and tobacco quit within the last 5 years count as such a combination, and if so what is added for it?
